sense: a copy of a text; to copy out

terms.gloss: a copy, transcript (of a letter or text)
evidence: Cic. Att. 8.6.1: deinde supposuit exemplum epistolae Domitiī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A copy made from an original; the original itself is exemplar or archetypum.

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: ex aliquō exscrībere
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.189: tabulās in forō summā hominum frequentiā exscrībō (Lewis & Short)
Gell. 3.3.8: ex Plautī cōmoediā duōs versūs exscrīpsimus (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 28: clandestīnō exscrībere, to copy by cheating
terms.comment: “Don’t copy from your neighbour!” is Nōlī exscrībere ex proximō! (Traupman 33).

sources: Lewis & Short: exemplum · Lewis & Short: exscribo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 28, checked against the searchable text of the book.: p. 297; p. 286; p. 289.
